coaching.headline: Up twenty-five kills to nineteen, later two enemy inhibitors down, and the team still gave up the last nine kills and the Core. Fucking thrown.
coaching.team: The enemy scored the first three kills before the team drew blood, then the team climbed to a twenty-five to nineteen lead. The team took eight structures including two inhibitors, nineteen river buffs to twelve, the Mini Prime, the first Primal Fangtooth and the Orb Prime. The enemy took two of three Fangtooths and the second Primal Fangtooth. Then the enemy scored the last nine kills of the game and went from three allied outer towers to the Core.
coaching.lossReflection: The lead needed spending, not more coin-flip fights. The alternative: once the first enemy inhibitor fell, group all five behind an allied minion wave for the next structure, and treat any allied death as the signal to back off until that player respawns. Steel died outside any detected fight and the next fight went 2-3; four allies later died in the Orb Prime window. No plan guarantees the win, but this one ended with nine straight allied deaths.

focus.title: Spend the inhibitor lead with five
focus.action: From the first enemy inhibitor on, one player names the next structure and the team walks in only with all five up. Next game, count allied deaths after the first enemy inhibitor falls; this game had twelve.

15.5.call: Legion killed Renna and Lt. Belica killed Serath; Sparrow killed Legion and Steel killed Muriel. The fight went 3-1 and the team took the Fangtooth less than a minute later. Legion and Steel both scored away from home lanes before either lane had opened.

34.4.call: Sparrow killed Steel and Serath killed Kira with no enemy deaths. Within the next minute the team took the enemy duo-lane inner tower and inhibitor, and the enemy took the second Primal Fangtooth. The record cannot show whether the two deaths decided that Primal Fangtooth.

36.6.call: Renna killed Legion and Lt. Belica, Sparrow killed Aurora and Serath killed Steel, with no enemy deaths, while the team took the Orb Prime. The kills fell on opposite sides of the map, two separate plays rather than one fight. Shortly after, the enemy took two inner towers, an inhibitor and the Core.

2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e.matchup: The lane opponent was Terra: Wild Rush is Unstoppable while channeling and knocks back on impact, Highland Hurl shreds physical armor and slows (roots when Empowered), and Unstoppable Force cleanses debuffs, disables nearby towers and adds both armors and tenacity. Terra killed Legion three times and finished with the most damage mitigated in the game. Terra's Tainted Guard also cuts the healing of anyone who basic-attacks Terra, which matters for a rifle hero. Across the match, Serath's dives and Renna's Stupor mesmerize were the other threats.
2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e.build: On the winning core of Malady, Deathstalker and Spear Of Desolation, plus Viper, The Perforator and Mesmer. Every item carries physical penetration, which also raises the rifle's damage per point, and the totals clear the Ballistic Calibration thresholds that lengthen the Saturation Charge slow and widen Orbital Sanction. Deathstalker's shred, Viper's Corrode and The Perforator's armor ignore all cut into Terra's armor. Spear Of Desolation adds ultimate haste and damage after casting Orbital Sanction, and Mesmer adds health and a spell shield that blocks the next ability.
2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e.eternal: Thraex marks the last enemy hero Legion's basic attacks damaged, raising damage against that hero and reducing the damage that hero deals back, which suits a rifle that keeps firing on one target. Savage Strikes adds on-hit damage that heals, though Terra's Tainted Guard cuts that healing whenever Legion shoots Terra. Rallying Roar adds ultimate haste and gives nearby allies movement speed when Orbital Sanction is cast. Golden Mane is the draft alternative to Rallying Roar: less damage taken from non-area attacks and abilities, giving up the group speed burst.
2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e.augment: Scorched Earth makes Frag Order and the Saturation Charge mines leave napalm zones, and Orbital Sanction drops one every half second. The burn pays when enemies hold ground, such as around an objective, and adds little against a target that walks out. Press the Advantage is the alternative: a takedown spawns a Rally Point at the fallen target that raises Legion's rate of fire and ally attack speed, giving up the napalm and the Rally Point heal.
2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e.crest: Ortus is an offensive burst: for a short window Legion gains movement speed and physical power, and a takedown inside that window adds permanent physical power and refreshes the window. The crest also carries physical penetration for the rifle. Ortus offers no defense, so against Terra's engage the speed works as a chase or reposition tool rather than protection. Activations are not recorded.
2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e.improvement: Seven deaths and no completed item with armor, while Terra, Serath and Sparrow deal mostly physical damage. If Terra or Serath keep ending exchanges first, Draconum in place of Viper is the comparison: physical power, physical armor, ability haste and healing on takedowns, giving up Viper's attack speed, physical penetration, armor shred and bonus damage against shredded targets. Mesmer is a sound keep, since the spell shield can block Renna's Stupor or Terra's Highland Hurl.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.matchup: Duo was Steel and Kira against Sparrow and Muriel. Sparrow ramps damage through Relentless stacks and can vanish into stealth with Heightened Senses; Muriel's fully charged Serenity stuns, and Reversal Of Fortune flies to any ally for a shield and damage reduction, knocking up enemies on arrival. Steel killed Sparrow three times, the most by any ally. Renna killed Steel three times, more than either duo opponent, and Serath killed Kira five times.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Steel brought the anti-heal: Tainted Charm cuts healing on any enemy hero near Steel and slows that hero, which covers Muriel's heals and Serath, who had the most healing in the game. Tainted Guard cuts the healing of anyone basic-attacking Steel, such as Serath or Sparrow. Fire Blossom, Tainted Guard and Vainglory stack physical armor, which feeds Heavy Metal's bonus damage. Raiment of Renewal's regeneration only runs out of combat. Vainglory is the only item with magical armor, against Renna's magical damage.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Krix scales the health that Raiment of Renewal, Tainted Charm and Fire Blossom stack. Voracity heals a little and pays a little gold on each unit kill, and Cannibalism adds permanent health per takedown; with fourteen takedowns, that paid steadily. Regenerative Tissue is the draft alternative to Voracity: regeneration after a stretch without hero damage instead of per-kill healing. Festering Wounds adds little here, since Steel already carried two anti-heal items.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.augment: Heavy Metal adds magical damage to heavy punches and Shield Bash based on Steel's total physical and magical armor, so every armor item feeds the bonus. Adaptive Force is the alternative against a ranged lineup of Sparrow, Renna and Muriel: two Force Shield charges on a shorter cooldown at a smaller size, more projectile blocks, giving up the armor-based damage.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.crest: Rift Walkers dashes and pulls nearby heroes toward Steel, an engage that sets up Shield Bash or Shield Slam, and adds passive gold and a third ward slot. Steel placed the most wards in the game, though totals cannot show how often the extra slot was in use. Against Serath on Kira, the pull can drag a diver off the carry; activations are not recorded.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves, and Steel built none of the three. Xenia is the clearest comparison with a carry dying to Serath: a shield on any ally standing right beside Steel plus both armors, giving up Raiment of Renewal's larger health pool, health regeneration, tenacity, some ability haste and the out-of-combat regeneration. The record cannot show which of Kira's deaths a shield would have changed.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: The jungle opponent was Serath, tied for the most kills in the game and with the most healing. Heaven's Fury vanishes and strikes the marked target while immune to crowd control and invulnerable, and every takedown drops a visage that grants Heresy at no cost on touch. Aurora's roots and the Cryoseism stun land once Serath reappears, not during the dash. Terra's Unstoppable Force cleanses debuffs and Wild Rush is Unstoppable while channeling, so control spent into those windows is wasted.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: On the winning core of Spirit Of Amir, Magnify and Spectral Schematics, plus Dynamo, Elafrost and Flux Matrix. Spectral Schematics and Dynamo both trigger on immobilizing an enemy, which Hoarfrost's root, the Glacial Thorns crystals and the Cryoseism stun supply. Flux Matrix halves the tenacity of nearby enemy heroes and makes those heroes take more magical damage, a direct answer to the tenacity from Terra's Unstoppable Force. Dynamo and Elafrost add physical armor and Flux Matrix adds magical armor, so the defense covers both damage types.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Lotus grants a small random bonus every two minutes and on each takedown, and eleven takedowns fed Lotus. Flawless heals Aurora and nearby allies once per cast when an ability hits an enemy hero, and Fragrance adds magical damage against heroes close by; both suit a jungler who fights inside spell range. Immaculate is the draft alternative to Fragrance: damage reduction while near full health, giving up the close-range damage.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Glacial Thorns makes Glacial Charge leave crystals that damage and root, an extra immobilize for Dynamo and Spectral Schematics. Hypothermia is the alternative against this lineup: Boreal Sweep hits on heroes cut both armors and slow attack speed, which Sparrow and Serath both lean on, giving up the extra root and those item triggers.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Tempest deals damage to nearby heroes every second for a stretch and heals Aurora for part of that damage, so the crest pays when Aurora stays in contact for the full duration. Muriel's damaging abilities and Sparrow's Tainted Rounds can cut that healing. Activations are not recorded.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: Nothing in this match argues for a swap: two deaths and the winning core in place. Elafrost's empowered basic attack after a cast slows and hits harder against monsters, which suits the clear. If a later lobby has no tenacity or magical-damage target to answer, the Flux Matrix slot is the one to reconsider; here the item is a sound keep.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: The mid opponent was Renna: Mortal Coil pulls targets in, heals Renna and executes at low health, Stupor mesmerizes from a hover, and Abyssal Rift teleports Renna after a channel. Renna took first blood on Lt. Belica and killed Lt. Belica once more; Lt. Belica killed Renna three times. Renna spends mana on every active ability, so Void Drone's zaps and drain and the missing-mana damage on Neural Disruptor all have a target. Renna finished second in hero damage, behind Lt. Belica.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: On the winning core of Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings, then Oblivion Crown, Caustica and Megacosm. Noxia's bonus needs a separate ability to hit a marked hero, which Seismic Assault, Void Bomb and Neural Disruptor provide. Caustica ignores a share of magical armor, against Terra's Transference and Inquisition and Muriel's Devotion. Megacosm adds health and a burn that scales with bonus health, against Terra's health stacking. All six items add magical power and only Megacosm adds health: a pure output build.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Aion stacks mana regeneration on casts and turns spell damage on enemy heroes into gold. With the most hero damage in the game, the gold half had plenty to feed on, and Lt. Belica finished second in gold in the game. Runic Focus adds magical power while mana stays high, and Bottomless Vial pays a potion charge and permanent magical power per river buff killed. Philosopher is the draft alternative to Bottomless Vial: steady passive gold that does not depend on taking river buffs.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Combat Veteran adds a little movement speed and passive experience over time, pure scaling with no fight effect. Devastating Bombs is the fight-side alternative: Void Bomb hits harder on an isolated target, giving up the experience and speed.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Soulbearer grants a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed for a window, a self-sustain tool for a hero with no dash beyond Blink. Sparrow's Tainted Rounds can cut the lifesteal half, so the shield is the part that buys time against Sparrow and Serath. Activations are not recorded.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: Hold the core: hero damage per minute more than double the recorded Lt. Belica norm says the output landed. The only gap is defense, with no item adding armor. If Serath or Sparrow start ending fights before the second spell, Golem's Gift in place of Megacosm is the comparison: more magical power, physical armor, mana regeneration and ability haste, giving up Megacosm's health and the maximum-health and bonus-health burns. If Renna is the problem, magical armor is the comparison instead.

c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8.matchup: Duo was Kira and Steel against Sparrow and Muriel. Kira killed Sparrow twice and Muriel once, and Sparrow killed Kira once. The bigger threat was Serath, who killed Kira five times: Heaven's Fury vanishes and strikes the marked target while immune to crowd control, and Chastise slows. During Purge, Kira moves slowly and can cast nothing but Shadow Glide, so a channel started with Serath unseen leaves one exit.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8.build: An all-crit basic-attack build: Onixian Quiver fires extra projectiles, Dust Devil stacks attack speed on hero hits, Imperator boosts critical damage, Demolisher ignores physical armor and Terminus turns excess lifesteal healing into a shield. No item adds armor or health. Terra's Tainted Guard cuts the healing of anyone basic-attacking Terra, so shooting Terra starves the lifesteal that Terminus needs.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8.eternal: Vermis adds maximum-health damage on every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero, Serration adds missing-health damage to that hit, and Melting Point adds damage only against heavily armored targets. Terra's three physical armor items alone pass that threshold; the rest of the enemy lineup built little or no physical armor. Sub-Surface is the draft alternative to Melting Point: less damage from area abilities such as Hail Of Arrows and Heresy, giving up the bonus against Terra.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8.augment: Bringer Of Mercy makes Mercy cheaper and cuts Kira's current ability cooldowns each time Mercy deals damage, so Shadow Glide comes back sooner in a long fight. Siphoning Purge is the sustain alternative, healing off Purge damage to heroes, giving up those cooldown cuts; Muriel's damaging abilities reduce enemy healing and would eat into that option.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8.crest: Pacifier is a second dash beside Shadow Glide and Blink, and the empowered hit applies to Kira's physical damage. Against Serath, the dash is the escape the build otherwise lacks. Activations are not recorded, so whether the crest was ready in any of the ten deaths is unknown.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8.improvement: The winning core is Solaris, Ashbringer and Imperator; Kira had Imperator. Ashbringer in place of Dust Devil is the comparison against Serath: each basic attack cuts current non-ultimate cooldowns, so Shadow Glide returns faster, giving up Dust Devil's movement speed, some attack speed and the stacking attack speed and speed from Menace. The record cannot show which of the ten deaths a faster Shadow Glide would have changed.

2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e: Legion played the offlane like a siege engine: the enemy offlane outer tower and inhibitor both fell to Legion, and both trips to mid before the lane opened scored a kill, the second paying off with the team's Fangtooth.

Seven deaths ran over the recorded Legion norm, three to Terra, one outside any detected fight. When Terra lands Wild Rush, Legion answers with Rally Point: the knockback buys room and the standard heals allies who stay close.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 did the support job on Steel: the most wards placed and cleared in the game, no deaths before the ten-minute mark, a hand in over half the team's kills and a mid-lane kill on Muriel that paid off.

Five deaths sat over the recorded Steel norm, three to Renna, and one outside any detected fight came before a fight that went 2-3. Soulfire fires projectile waves, so Steel parks Force Shield between Renna and the backline.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster ran a heavy jungle game on Aurora: the most objective damage in the game, farm well over the recorded Aurora norm and the fewest deaths on the team. Clean as fuck.

The objective trade still leaked: the enemy took two of three Fangtooths and the second Primal Fangtooth, and four wards placed sat well under the recorded Aurora norm. Before each Fangtooth, Aurora calls the timer and where Serath last showed.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim was the standout of this lobby on Lt. Belica: the most hero damage in the game, tied with Serath for the most kills, and hero damage per minute more than double the recorded Lt. Belica norm. Filthy.

Once the enemy mid outer tower fell, Lt. Belica took three kills on the duo lane, each followed within a minute and a half by an enemy structure falling. With mid open, Lt. Belica keeps walking to duo-lane fights.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8: Ten deaths, the most in the game, and Serath took five. Twoattack farmed well over the recorded Kira norm and took down the enemy duo outer tower, but the carry spent the game as Serath's favorite fucking snack.

One death to Serath outside any detected fight landed less than a minute before the enemy's first Fangtooth. With Serath unseen, Kira starts Purge only with Steel close: the channel leaves Shadow Glide as the only castable ability.

threats: Heal-stacking: Muriel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 1 item of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

ourKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
ourKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
ourKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
ourKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Alacrity shield+AS → Consecrated Ground bubble → Reversal global save
enemyKits.winCondition: keep the carry alive with global shields and enable their damage
enemyKits.passive: abilities grant Sentinel to allies; on-hit bonus
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has no damage threat — dive her carry through the shields or pick her first

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Wild Rush charge → Ruthless Assault → Highland Hurl slow → Unstoppable Force cleanse ult
enemyKits.winCondition: engage Unstoppable and grind with Hersir-empowered swings
enemyKits.passive: Hersir stacks empower the next basic
enemyKits.playAgainst: save CC for after Unstoppable Force; kite her charge

enemyKits.combo: Soulfire waves → Mortal Coil pull-zone → Stupor orb → Abyssal Rift zone
enemyKits.winCondition: zone a fight with Mortal Coil + ult and chunk from range
enemyKits.passive: consumes essences from kills for power
enemyKits.playWith: frontline to hold enemies in her zones
enemyKits.playAgainst: fragile and reliant on her zones — flank/dive around the telegraphs
